meta.topStoryHeadline: Seven Black Creatives and Scholars Named 2026 MacArthur Fellows
meta.topStorySummary: The 2026 MacArthur class recognizes artists, writers, a jazz musician, a choreographer, and an economist among seven Black fellows. Each receives an unrestricted $800,000 fellowship over five years.
executiveSummary: The 2026 MacArthur Fellows include seven Black creatives and scholars, with recognition spanning jazz, dance, visual art, fiction, and economics. Nyancho NwaNri receives the Flickr × Black Women Photographers grant.

Museum labor negotiations have split: Whitney workers set an October 5 strike date, while Brooklyn Museum and American Folk Art Museum unions reach tentative agreements. Lawmakers introduce a bill to protect the Kennedy Center from demolition after an expedited Senate effort is blocked.

Kyle Abraham’s renamed company pairs a new identity with year-round dancer pay and royalties. Jocelyn Bioh’s School Girls opens on Broadway, Shuffle Along’s reunion will reach PBS in 2027, and a new exhibition examines Edmonia Lewis’s Montana connections.
meta.newsDisplayModel: 1 main top story, 7 photo highlights, remaining current-week stories text-only, August 2026 onward in archive
meta.eventsCarryForwardNote: Updated from the September 30 Radar. Started events use their closing month and show Through dates; future events use their opening month. Listings without a confirmed closing month appear under Dates to confirm. Still-current prior listings are retained; expired events and duplicate listings are removed.
meta.calendarDateRule: end month after an event starts; start month before it starts

events.title: In Praise of Divas: Mariah Carey and Whitney Houston
events.description: Emily Lordi (Holding Lightning: The Life, Loves, and Art of Whitney Houston) and Andrew Chan. A new Whitney Houston biography that treats her as a self-directed musician, launched at an independent bookstore with a wine reception.

events.title: Studio Museum Fall Member Preview
events.dates: Wed, Sept 30, 11 AM–6 PM and 6:30–9 PM
events.description: 2026 Artists in Residence and permanent collection installations. Worth a membership on its own if members want first access to the fall season.

events.title: Terrance Hayes and Kyle Carrero Lopez
events.venue: The Poetry Project, St. Mark's Church
events.description: Terrance Hayes, Kyle Carrero Lopez, introduced by Simone White. A MacArthur Fellow and National Book Award winner reads at one of the city's longest-running poetry venues, for $10.

events.title: A Sustained Becoming: Studio Museum Artists in Residence 2026
events.description: Derriann Pharr, Simonette Quamina, Taylor Simmons. The first residency cohort to work in the museum's new building shows new work.

events.title: Armstrong in Ghana
events.description: Louis Armstrong's travels and legacy in Ghana. A new archival exhibition on Armstrong's connection to Ghana.

events.title: Bill Chats
events.description: Bill T. Jones, Joanna Kotze, and guests. Bill T. Jones in open conversation, a standing series that rarely gets the attention it deserves.

events.title: Claudia Rankine Discusses Triage with Hala Alyan
events.venue: Brooklyn Public Library, Central Library, Dweck Center
events.description: Claudia Rankine, Hala Alyan. A free chance to hear the author of Citizen on her new collection, two weeks before her BAM conversation.

events.title: creation stories and all the important importants
events.venue: Lincoln Center Theater, LCT3 Claire Tow Theater
events.description: Written by Mfoniso Udofia, directed by Tamilla Woodard. A Nigerian American playwright's LCT3 debut, centering a midlife Black woman moving between her many selves.

events.title: Harlem Chamber Players: Hispanic Heritage Month Celebration
events.description: The Harlem Chamber Players (Claire Chan, Ashley Horne, William Frampton, Wayne Smith); works by Tania León, Paquito D'Rivera, Arriaga, Turina, and a world premiere of Ignacio Rosado's revised and completed quartet. Harlem's own chamber ensemble plays Afro-Cuban composer Tania León and a world premiere, free, among the museum's galleries.

events.title: Harlem Quartet at Sugar Hill
events.venue: Five Boroughs Music Festival at Sugar Hill Museum of Art + Storytelling
events.description: Harlem Quartet; program includes William Grant Still's Lyric Quartette and music by Wynton Marsalis. A Grammy-winning quartet plays the "Dean of African American composers" alongside Beethoven, free, in a small Harlem museum.

events.title: Harry Belafonte's Uptown Life and Legacies
events.venue: Word Up Community Bookshop, at Recirculation
events.description: Joshua Jelly-Schapiro on Daylight Come: Harry Belafonte and the World He Made. A new biography of Belafonte's performing life and activism, discussed uptown at a volunteer-run neighborhood bookshop.

events.title: Works in Progress: Maheder Haileselassie
events.description: Maheder Haileselassie, Ethiopian artist and 2025 Counter Histories Fellow, with writer Maaza Mengiste. An Ethiopian artist reworks colonial archives of Italy's occupation of Ethiopia, in conversation with the author of The Shadow King.

events.title: Brooklyn Poets Poetry Festival
events.venue: Brooklyn Poets, 144 Montague Street and Zoom
events.description: Tina Chang, Cornelius Eady, Tongo Eisen-Martin, Angel Nafis, Natalie Diaz, and others. A small literary nonprofit's weekend of readings, panels, and workshops.

events.title: First Novel Friday
events.description: Deesha Philyaw (The True Confessions of First Lady Freeman), Bobuq Sayed, Ankur Thakkar. A celebrated short story writer's debut novel gets an early public reading.

events.title: New York City Ballet: Contemporary Choreography I
events.venue: David H. Koch Theater, Lincoln Center
events.description: Jennifer Archibald’s new ballet joins Kyle Abraham’s Love Letter (on shuffle) and work by Alysa Pires and Justin Peck. Performances are October 2, 4, 6 and 14.

events.title: African American Literary Awards Show
events.venue: Schomburg Center for Research in Black Culture
